The farewell to one of the best game franchises of last generation. It’s a good thing that another entry is just around the corner.

Mass Effect 3 is obviously the most visually appealing of the series so far, which makes sense since it came out in 2012. The pre-rendered cutscenes all look pretty damn amazing for a five year old game from a previous generation. Most of my time spent with the game made me forget that I was playing an Xbox 360 game on my PC. 

So with so many outcomes possible I'd really recommend those coming into RPG games for the first time or maybe fell in love with games like Skyrim or the Witcher.

[h1]Flawed Masterpiece[/h1]

I originally skipped Mass Effect 3 because of all the flak it took for being "no Mass Effect anymore" etc. Now I've picked up on the "Digital Deluxe Edition" featuring all DLCs I'm glad I did - because it's brilliant. Even though it's botched.

[b]THE GOOD[/b]
- Offers the quirky characters and dialogue everyone's come to love from the series
- The distinct art design and impeccable sound design make for some truly formidable moments and greatly contribute to recreating the "Mass Effect"-feel once again
- Reunions with characters from ME1 and ME2 and references to what happened before in the former games help create the feel of an epic space opera filled with a history of its own
- Even though straying from the classic quasi-turn-based game mechanics, pausable combat still gives it a tactical feel not too far from its predecessors, powers and weapons offer plenty of variety
- Most importantly, ME3 succeeds in what's probably every RPGs core challenge: To create a disctinct, fascinating world that seems real and alive in which you can get lost, filled with interesting characters some of which you will miss once the credits have rolled.
- The Digital Deluxe Edition (featuring the DLCs) offers varied missions and interesting settings that kept me invested in ME3s world until the end.
- Offers a spectacular finale truly worthy of the beloved space opera it brings to a satisfying close.

[b]THE BAD[/b]
- Has its fair share of stereotypical "US Marines in space"-bull, including constant saluting and "Yes Sir!"-ing, more motivational speeches than "Top Gun", a soundtrack full of marching drums and mission briefings that keep inviting you to "kick some ass!". I wouldn't have cared if this was Quake or Doom, but with the "Mass Effect" series, sentences like "The cavalry has arrived!" or "We had a nuke - and we intended to use it." just somehow didn't sit right. You can even gain at "Patriot"-accomplishment if you make it till the end.
- some similarly stereotypical depictions of nationality/race - most obviously and annoyingly with your squadmate Vega, who's introduced as the cliché "latino" and of course is talking about what's "loco", who's a "pendejo" and who's got the biggest "cojones" all the time (if he's not lifting weights or hitting on girls, that is).
- The combat- and movement system has been much criticized, and rightfully so. I've always found "Gears of War"'s movement system to be simply terrible, and ME3 practically makes a carbon copy of it. Running feels like your driving a London double-decker bus on glazed streets with a broken off steering wheel. Also, the mechanics for taking cover makes you feel like you are trying to travers a world covered in velvet - dressed in a velcro suit. You will constantly find yourself sticking to random objects you never wanted to take cover behind.
- Especially, assigning the same key to "use", "sprint", "take cover", "climb", "jump across" and "evade" really, really, really doesn't make things better. More than once, I found myself in front of a terminal I wanted Shepard to use and something like this happened: I press the corresponding key. She takes cover behind it. I remove her from the wall, press again. She takes a dive roll away from it. I get back to the terminal and press again. She climbs over the terminal. While initially this makes for some comedic value, it grows more infuriating over time.
- terrible quest management system that doesn't allow collapsing or prioritizing missions, doesn't update quest status if you've completed parts of the mission and makes you lose track of the (many) sidequests quickly and that keeps unfinished quests that have become unfinishable stick to your quest list anyway.
- the map is similarly terrible: Looking for a certain planet for a scan? You'll, have to randomly check on all the systems available hoping to find it in the end. Of course, the map also doesn't mention where you'll find fuel depots which you'll need, because you'll need to refuel in order to traverse space (a mechanism by the way which serves no ludic purpos whatsoever except for artificially stretching playtime).
- many sidequests consist solely of finding a certain planet (which is often hindered by the confusing map) and pushing a key to scan it. Also, it should be noted that, while I really like mini-games in RPGs, the planet-scanning-minigame of Mass Effect is so remarkably bland and boring I'd hardly consider it a "game" at all. Is it a game if you follow an arrow on your crosshairs until you find a spot and klick on it? Still, this is the most prominent (and constantly repeated) mini-game of ME3.
- Without spoiling anything about the ending, a formal element that irritated me was that after a very long, visually spectacular and fittingly epic series finale, the game ends with.. a series of stills with off-commentary what happens?? Let's just say that this felt oddly anticlimactic.

[b]THE BUGGY[/b]
- It has been said before, but let me state it again: ME3, even 8 years after its release, really is full of bugs. I found none of them to be completely game-breaking, but let me list those I came across for the sake of thoroughness: repeated crashes; repeated freezes; severe FPS-drops until I used a community-made fix that kills the origin overly that seems to cause this; avatar repeatedly stuck to certain positions after dialogues and couldn't be moved any more - until you started mashing on the movement buttons repeatedly; in-game emails disappeared after having been read; the order of in-game emails was randomly changed, making older mails reappear on top of the list; got stuck in a combat arena situation because the game didn't notice that all enemies had been killed off; lines of dialogue repeatedly broke off unfinished.

[b]CONCLUSION[/b]
While the multitude of its kinks and quirks may make it seem as if ME3 is a bad game, surprisingly, the opposite is true. Despite all it's minor flaws, the game gets all the things very right that are at the center of what made the ME-trilogy great: Interesting characters and dialogue, fascinating and varied worlds and complex relations between alien races, lush art design and the overall feel of being in a universe all its own - probably for the last time. ME3 succeeds in making the trilogy stand out as one of the few definitive space operas in the history of gaming.
After a few texture mods and tweaks i really enjoyed this game and over all was a great series. just wish i hadn't waited for so long to play.

The ending is the same no matter what you choose. That's why they're all upset. The theme of the series has always been decisions and consequences and Bioware has promised that all choices in the series would have a decisive impact, but ultimately they do not affect nickles about how the story ends. Another thing that made me crazy was where was the happy ending?
I am a man of culture I like happy endings!

The final big choice? Decide the color of the last cutscene. This game breaks the trilogy! 
7\10.
